scope: Trading-lane research convergence of 13 layers (12 catalog trading layers plus strategy-research) from the user's starred repositories, 8 awesome lists and per-layer candidate research, each layer proposal challenged by a cross-family GPT-6 refutation. Inclusion is not installation, E2E or superiority; no selection changes here. Inputs for the verdict wave alongside catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260926.json.

companion_record.relation: The landscape sweep's manifest covers 11 of these layers (security-supply-chain as a foundation layer; strategy-research is trading-only). Candidates here use its trading candidate shape; the verdict wave takes both records as inputs.

method.review: Per layer: Claude candidate research, adversarial claim checks (claude-verify) and a proposal (winner status, challengers with trial plans, rejections). Workers ran Claude Sonnet at effort max on 2026-09-26.
method.cross_family: GPT-6 (gpt-6-astra, model_reasoning_effort max, codex exec 0.157.1, read-only sandbox) asked to refute each proposal against primary sources. Lens gpt-6-cached ran with the client default search (external_web_access false, per evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260926/codex/results/websearch-0.157.1.json); lens gpt-6-live ran with -c web_search="live". All 13 layers have a live vote; 8 also have a cached vote.
method.mapping: One Claude Opus mapper per layer (effort max, no web) attributed each vote to candidates and winners with a verbatim quote; this builder dropped every vote whose quote did not match its source text.
method.survives_rule: survives=false when any kept vote refutes the label or claim; true when at least one kept GPT-6 vote addresses it and none refutes; null (disposition *_unverified) when no kept GPT-6 vote addresses it. Dispositions follow manifest-20260923's vocabulary.

trading.claude_summary:
Judged strictly on verified (supported) evidence, none of the 15 researched candidates reaches native_execution-level proof of being better than the three incumbents on this stack's own tasks. The layer's own repeated finding stands even after this sweep: "No non-adopted candidate in this packet has retained comparative evidence sufficient to prefer it" (conv/layers.json open_gaps, and independently corroborated in catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json's uncited_claims/next_steps). Recommendation is add_candidates, not a bare keep and not challenge: register one concrete, evidence-backed trial candidate (Claude Agent SDK) for the sdk/native-workers facet, log two genuinely new-to-this-repo finds as tracked references, and fix two verified pin-hygiene gaps the sweep surfaced.

Winner-by-winner (verified directly against repo files, not just the researcher's paraphrase): codex-native-sdk's recorded pin (CLI rust-v0.155.1 / PyPI openai-codex 0.154.0) is genuinely stale -- gh api and PyPI JSON, both dated 2026-09-26, show 4 non-prerelease CLI releases (156.0, 156.1, 157.0, 157.1) and 5 PyPI releases (155.1, 156.0, 156.1, 157.0, 157.1) have shipped since the pin (the packet's "two releases behind" claim is refuted; the real gap is larger). I independently read catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json and found this pin already flagged pin_behind_upstream on 2026-09-23 -- the gap has been open and widening for at least three days -- and manifests/stack.json's own version field (read directly) still says "0.155.1" with no cutover note, unlike ai-memory's entry. This is a live operational lag, not paperwork; status: stale. foundation-ai-memory's catalog pin text (v2.3.1, in both conv/layers.json and catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json) is stale by three upstream releases (latest v2.4.1, 2026-09-25), but manifests/stack.json's version field, read directly, already says "2.4.1" with a dated freshness note describing an approved, rehearsed cutover on this host "since 2026-09-26" -- independently corroborated by this session's own memory index line ("ai-memory 2.4.1 switched (#291, #307)"). The operational component matches upstream HEAD; only the two catalog pin fields need a refresh commit. No alternative (Mem0/Hindsight/Graphiti/Cognee/Letta Code/Supermemory) has matched-task evidence against it, so status: earns_it. foundation-socraticode is one release behind (v1.14.0 vs v1.15.0 -- an exact +1 gap per gh api, zero intervening tags), a gap that only opened in the last two days (the 09-23 sweep still showed v1.14.0 as upstream-current) and is a recorded, deliberate user deferral (">=10-01" per this session's memory index), not neglect; repo remains actively pushed (2026-09-24). No alternative conceptual-code-search candidate was proposed or verified; status: earns_it.

Highest-priority unfinished action, ahead of any external candidate: catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json's own verdict_overturn_when already fully specifies (exact CLI commands with file:line citations) a same-task, matched-budget trial across codex-native-sdk, DeerFlow-via-codex-acp and OmniRoute. Preliminary, uncontrolled numbers in conv/layers.json's open_gaps look favorable to the DeerFlow/codex-acp arm (1 of 1 tasks completed, 0 blocked, 42,345 cumulative tokens, vs. codex-native-sdk's 1 of 3 completed, 2 blocked, up to 204,091 tokens) -- but that same source explicitly disqualifies the comparison ("c19 read files with head -c, while c20's task required Context Mode extraction, so the numbers are not comparable"). This is not a verified advantage, so codex-acp/DeerFlow and OmniRoute stay in "rejected" rather than "challengers" -- but running the already-specified trial is the single cheapest, most-ready next step in the whole packet.

Rejections were made on today's own verified facts, not incumbency: OpenAI Agents SDK's cadence (last tag 09-17, nine days before this check) trails both Codex's own upstream and Claude Agent SDK's near-daily cadence, and this repo's own prior source_review (catalogs/us-equities/agents-operations.json, checked 2026-09-19) already notes it needs a wholly separate, metered OpenAI API entitlement, not the existing Codex subscription flow -- so it was rejected, not promoted, despite also being an official first-party SDK. Complementary lanes not formally in winners[] but worth noting: Serena's installed version (2.0.0.dev0 @ c6fbd1c5, per manifests/stack.json) differs from its catalogued pin (v1.7.0) and carries a split MIT (SolidLSP) / GPL-3.0-or-later (application) license; QMD showed a fresh, dated live-status call today. Neither is a rejected candidate -- both are adopted infrastructure -- so neither appears in winner_status (scoped to the three formal winners[] entries) or rejected.

Two 2026 papers (InKH, arXiv:2606.01886; KTD-Fin, arXiv:2605.28359) speak directly to this layer's own retrieval-quality-measurement gap but have no located public code (confirmed absent from every catalog/manifest file grepped), so they are tracked as method references for the layer's own preregistered held-out trial, not as installable candidates or rejections. TradeMemory Protocol is the most literally on-point new find (financial-agent memory with an audit trail) but is self-declared "feature-complete, in maintenance mode... no new features... planned" -- rejected as a frozen design reference, not a growing contender.

Paper-lane impact across this entire layer is none: every candidate here sits in the research/memory/worker-SDK lane, which this repo's own policy (blueprints/us-equities/workers/policy.md: "no orders or credential stores") and north-star rule ("models stay in research"; paper orders go only through the separate deterministic adaptive-paper engine) wall off from engines-run, paper-acts-passed and paper-fills counts.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The only advantage claimed is freshness and maintenance, and the proposal says outright that it is not a claim of functional superiority. v0.2.160 was released on 2026-09-25 as a same-day GitHub tag and PyPI upload about a minute apart, and releases come almost daily. candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Trial: first confirm a sanctioned SDK authentication route, since Anthropic docs prohibit wiring a personal claude.ai/Claude Code login into an automated third-party product without prior approval, and do not reuse native OAuth stores. Then install claude-agent-sdk==0.2.160 in an isolated venv and run the exact frozen c20 fixture from blueprints/us-equities/workers/receipt.json and policy.md (same prompt, 180s deadline, read_only sandbox) through claude_agent_sdk, writing a receipt in the same schema. PASS: match c20's one successful research-task result and also complete the two currently-blocked file-extraction follow-ups, under an equally strict read-only sandbox, at equal or lower total and failed-attempt token counts than the c20 baseline (135,311 tokens for the completed task; 204,091 across all three turns with 2 blocked). OVERTURN: any of (a) failure to enforce the same read-only boundary, (b) a need for materially broader tool, file or network scope, (c) inability to clear the authentication approval gate, or (d) worse completion or token results than c20 on the identical frozen task.

trading.claude_summary: Both current winners still earn their roles on convergent, dated, native_execution-level evidence — reconfirmed today via three independent authoritative sources in the checkout (layers.json, catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json, catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json) plus my own fresh gh api/PyPI/LICENSE reads that match the researcher's and adversarial-verifier's figures almost exactly (e.g., nautilustrader pushed_at today 2026-09-26T14:16:50Z, 29,420 stars vs. their 29,418-29,419; LEAN NuGet channel independently re-confirmed real vs. the misleading 2017-dated GitHub Releases page). No candidate among the 15 surveyed (evidence levels ranging metadata → source_review → native_execution) offers verified proof of a better alternative for either role, so the proposal is to KEEP both — but "keep" here is a statement about tool merit, not about requirement completion: layers.json's own decision for this layer stays "keep_but_compare" for good reason. The single most important finding, straight from the checkout's own authoritative gate record (not from the input research packet, which framed it more softly): the SPY/LEAN parity gate is currently BLOCKED (verdict.json, 4 failed checks; the one_zero scenario's native ending cash differs from LEAN by -655.12 USD). mapping-manifest.json names the two specific unsupported mechanics: market_on_open_proxy and distributions_and_cash. Source review (both the sota-convergence manifest and, independently, the earlier adversarial pass) confirms the underlying Rust mechanism a future fix would use — SimulationModule (crates/backtest/src/modules/mod.rs) and adjust_account (crates/backtest/src/exchange.rs:661) — genuinely exists at pin v2.0.0rc5, correcting an earlier internal claim (gates-20260922.json) that no such crediting mechanism existed; but the gate is still blocked end-to-end, so the mechanism existing in source is not the same as parity being achieved. The native MOO-fill gap is architectural, not a version lag: upstream issue #4063 was closed not_planned on 2026-05-15, so this cannot be fixed by simply upgrading Nautilus. No surveyed alternative closes this specific gap inside the NautilusTrader/IBKR destination architecture without abandoning the north star: hftbacktest has a source-confirmed (I read its own GitHub description directly) queue-position/latency fill model, but it targets crypto L2 microstructure, not US-equity MOO/distribution mechanics, so it doesn't actually address today's named blocker; csp and barter-rs are same-graph backtest=live architecture references worth remembering for the recurring IBKR-acceptance/continuous-paper-operation open_gap, but both would require a net-new brokerage adapter rather than a bounded trial; vectorbt/Backtesting.py/PyBroker are single-asset or ML-research tools out of scope for a broker-integrated destination engine; rqalpha's actual LICENSE (read directly, not via PyPI's misleading Apache-2.0 tag) blocks all organizational use without Ricequant's authorization; mementum/backtrader is the sweep's starkest stars-vs-merit mismatch (23,329 stars, 25+ months with zero commits, independently reconfirmed); and Vibe-Trading is the clearest "stars are not evidence" case (34k stars, 6 months old, pre-1.0, backtesting is 1 of 10 tags on an LLM agent product — and repository-index.md confirms it was deliberately starred as a test candidate for exactly this kind of check). One citation correction, independently resolved: the "six frozen SPY simulations" LEAN claim is real and native_execution-backed, but its correct primary source is catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json's own LEAN rationale plus blueprints/us-equities/historical-simulation/receipt.json — not catalogs/us-equities/coverage.json, which I read directly and confirmed is only a star-membership ledger with no such text (matching what the adversarial pass had already found). One new discovery beyond all input research: Hikyuu's actual repository LICENSE file is Apache License 2.0 (confirmed by reading the file), not MIT as both the researcher's candidate note and PyPI's own classifier state — a genuine license-metadata mismatch that changes no verdict here but is exactly the "beyond stars/classifier" nuance this exercise exists to catch. Net recommendation: no engine swap is warranted; the one concrete, bounded, paper-lane-relevant next step already implied by the repo's own evidence is closing the two named Nautilus-native gaps (MOO proxy fills, distribution-cash wiring) through the existing SimulationModule extension point on the current pin — that is native work on the winner, not a candidate trial, so it is not listed as a challenger.

trading.claude_summary:
Both winners verified real/unarchived/active via gh api 2026-09-26: dagu (github.com/dagucloud/dagu, pin v2.16.6) and data-pandera (github.com/unionai-oss/pandera, pin v0.33.1). Cross-checked the workflow's conv/layers.json extract against the repo's own catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json — consistent; the extract is a faithful derivation, not a fabricated citation (resolves a false-positive in the input packet's adversarial pass, which searched for a literal file named "layers.json" inside the repo checkout and found none).

PANDERA earns_it. Pin v0.33.1 is bit-for-bit current: gh api releases/latest and PyPI both show v0.33.1, GitHub published_at and PyPI upload_time both 2026-09-01 (independently verified, not just cited). Its fail-closed gate has now run against one real bounded Alpaca ingest — 24 symbols, 20 sessions, 2026-08-25 to 2026-09-22, 480 rows, 12/12 checks passing — gating one real paper trial on 2026-09-24 (gates-20260922.json "snapshot-promotion-gate" note and blueprints/us-equities/data/fixtures/good-gate-result.json, both read directly). That is more than the layer's own open_gaps text still says ("synthetic fixtures only" — stale). Its strongest challenger, Great Expectations (github.com/fivetran/great_expectations; genuine org-transfer from great-expectations/great_expectations confirmed independently via gh api, matching repo id 103071520, and separately by this repo's own manifest), was already source-reviewed by this repo's 2026-09-23 sota-convergence manifest (read directly, not just the packet's quotes) and correctly held back as heavier with "no demonstrated need," naming the exact unexecuted overturn test. I found no new evidence to overturn that.

DAGU is challenged, narrowly, on one axis. Upstream itself is healthy (4117 stars, GPL-3.0, pushed 2026-09-25) but the pin is 3 releases behind latest v2.17.2/2026-09-25 (independently reconfirmed via gh api, not just the packet's stale v2.17.0 citation), and manifest-20260923.json already names re-qualifying it on the newer release as a still-open internal action item. More structurally: this layer's requirement text explicitly asks for "recoverable state," and the same manifest cites a dedicated pin-qualification record (evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260923/pins-runtime/dagu.json) stating Dagu's in-flight self-healing is "inconclusive because no scheduler was started" — untested, not passed. trading.claude_summary: All three current winners -- data-mlflow (v3.16.1), inspect-ai (0.3.266), foundation-agent-retrieval-bench (v0.2.1) -- earn their status on freshly re-verified evidence, and this layer's recorded open_gaps/catalog text (conv/layers.json; catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json; catalogs/us-equities/{data-research,foundation-memory,agents-operations}.json) is stale: a pre-registered, hash-verified execution wave dated 2026-09-23 (evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/) already ran nearly every check the open_gaps still list as missing, three days before this review -- its own limits sections say updating the catalog text "is left to the coordinator." Most decisive: the exact promptfoo-vs-inspect-ai matched trial the open_gaps called for was run TWICE (an 8-case deterministic mock arm and a separate 30-case real-embedding-scorer arm) and settled both times with 100% cross-harness scoring agreement; inspect-ai edged ahead on frozen-source byte-fidelity (8/8 vs 6/8), self-contained retry-error provenance, and wall-clock. The project's own recorded verdict: "supports keeping inspect-ai selected... not a model-quality win." So promptfoo is not a verified challenger here -- merit, actually checked, favors the incumbent. mlflow was independently re-confirmed current (its README directly refutes comet-ml/opik's demonstrated_gap, matching the project's own 2026-09-23 adversarial verification) and shown bound to a real hash-verified replay of this project's own chronological research evaluation. foundation-agent-retrieval-bench's one recorded weakness (Darwin-arm64-only execution) was independently retired by a byte-identical Linux x86_64 rerun. Checked and correctly non-winning: opik (refuted), phoenix (Elastic-2.0 self-host restriction, narrower scope, already catalogued -- not a blind spot), river (real causality-probe-verified execution, but an honest negative predictive result), and three newly-surfaced small repos (TraderHarness/Lacuna/falsification-ledger) independently confirmed to exist but off-requirement for this layer (they validate trading-strategy backtests, not agent/experiment infrastructure -- fit backtesting-engine/strategy-research instead). Four 2026 papers confirmed real via direct abstract fetch are useful methodology inputs, not installable candidates. No verified challenger survives against any winner. Recommend only two low-cost housekeeping actions: bump the inspect-ai pin past 0.3.266 (already run successfully at 0.3.268 within this same wave; PyPI is now at 0.3.269) and have the coordinator refresh the stale catalog/open_gaps text to cite the 2026-09-23 receipts instead of describing these three winners as unexecuted.

trading.claude_summary: Most of this layer keeps its current picks on verified merit, not incumbency: NautilusTrader's engine pin, alpaca-py, and LEAN-as-oracle all reconfirm current/maintained/no-drift on 2026-09-26 primary sources. Reading current main (not just the frozen 2026-09-22 adjudication) resolves one open_gap and sharpens the other. (1) adaptive-paper-alpaca-adapter (c5) now earns_it: it passed a real native paper-broker trial on 2026-09-23 (5 orders, 4 fills, cash-reconciled) that did not exist at adjudication time, and it is the *only* Alpaca path into Nautilus, since NautilusTrader carries zero upstream Alpaca code (RFC nautechsystems/nautilus_trader#3374 open since 2026-01-01, PR #3375 closed unmerged same day). (2) nautilus-ibkr-adapter (c7) is genuinely challenged: I independently confirmed via `gh api` (2026-09-26) that github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader#4983 is still open, and its own title states the pinned v2.0.0rc5 Rust adapter's "execution client venue `IB` never matches instrument venue `SMART`, so every stock order is denied locally" -- a verified, currently-unpatched defect, not merely an untested boundary. The one visible fix candidate, PR #5041, is open/unmerged/"dirty" as of today. Meanwhile this repo's own receipt-20260923-passed.json shows the same project's older, non-pinned NautilusTrader 1.231.0 Python IBKR adapter already completing a real paper-Gateway accept/cancel/fill/flatten cycle with a reconciled-flat proof -- a zero-new-dependency interim path. Going beyond the given candidate list, per today's own alpaca-platform-landscape-20260926 artifact plus my direct gh api/PyPI checks: ml4t/backtest+data+live (MIT, pushed within the last 1-2 days, built-in LEAN-parity preset, same author lineage as this catalog's zipline-reloaded) is a fresher, better-licensed comparison-engine candidate than the already-catalogued Lumibot (GPL-3.0, reconfirmed) or StrateQueue (AGPL-3.0), worth a bounded parity trial using the existing frozen SPY fixture. Independently reconfirmed via `gh api`: LEAN's 17-commit drift beyond its pin is not capability-neutral as earlier framed -- it added combo orders (#9822) and OCO/OTO/OUO/bracket contingent orders (#9828, tests #9833) to LEAN's own Alpaca brokerage model.

trading.claude_summary: DVC (treeverse/dvc 3.67.1) keeps its win on the narrow claim it actually earns — versioned snapshot/restore — and the evidence for that claim got stronger, not weaker, since the 2026-09-22 gates file was written. The repo's own gap-wave-2 work (2026-09-23, evidence_class native_proven -> local_integration, 5 rounds of Codex+independent-Opus adversarial fixing) ran a real 4-way store comparison (baseline hash-manifest, DVC, PyIceberg 0.12.0, ArcticDB v6.26.0) on a materialized fixture: DVC and the baseline are the only arms that keep exact per-file sha256 (Iceberg/ArcticDB rewrite source files into their own formats, "not_supported by design"); under two concurrent writers, baseline/DVC/Iceberg lost 0 rows every time, but ArcticDB silently lost 50-150 of every 100-300 rows across repeated rounds -- confirming, by measurement rather than by license text alone, its own installed docstring's "concurrent writers to a single symbol are not supported" limitation. That, plus BSL-1.1 (source-available, forbids resale as a hosted "Database Service") and ~18x DVC's storage footprint on the same fixture, is a decisive strike against the researcher's ArcticDB pick. Iceberg is a genuine, verified trade-off (native time-travel, auto-retry concurrency safety, faster reads) but not a proven win -- it fails the byte-identical-snapshot bar the layer's requirement names, and needs an added catalog service; it stays "conditional," not promoted. Two of the layer's own seven listed open gaps are already closed by evidence layers.json/the 2026-09-22 adjudication have not caught up to: gap 4 ("no executed comparison measures... across the candidate stores") is settled by the comparison above, and gap 5/6 ("OpenLineage event persistence... and MLflow run-to-dataset bindings, remain unqualified") is settled by a 2026-09-23 local_integration run where openlineage-python 1.53.0 persisted schema-valid, tamper-detecting lineage events and mlflow 3.16.1 bound them to logged datasets -- directly contradicting both the researcher's own "UNEXECUTED"/"no receipt... wired" framing and the 2026-09-22 A/B adjudication that excluded OpenLineage from the winner set on exactly that (now outdated) basis. I therefore recommend adding OpenLineage+MLflow as a qualified lineage-persistence pairing (not displacing DVC, which was never meant to do this job). Separately, the catalog's own critic already flags foundation-socraticode as mis-tagged into this layer (it is a code-retrieval index, not a security-identity/provenance tool) -- a clean "demote, don't keep by default" finding I second. What remains a genuine, unclosed open_gap is the compound identity/corporate-action/licensing half of the requirement: the 235 ticker-collision and pre-2020-delisting gates are still not_established, and the repository's own 2026-09-23/09-26 sweeps already found and refuted every free OSS candidate they tried (BlackFalconData delisted-stocks-list, fja05680/sp500, stale Nasdaq Data Link). I independently WebFetched OpenFIGI's own API docs today and confirmed it is current-state mapping only (figi/ticker/name/exchCode/securityType fields; no listing/delisting date, no ticker-history, no active/inactive flag) -- it cannot resolve the 235 collisions, which need historical validity windows, not a permanent identifier. PermID's only Python client is 5.5 years stale and its coverage of this specific need is unverified, not confirmed. The only recorded viable closers (Databento, Sharadar -- explicitly not yet individually refuted by the 2026-09-23 sweep, QuantConnect Security Master/AlgoSeek, QuantRocket usstock) are all paid and explicitly gated as a user-decision, outside this read-only task's scope.

trading.claude_summary:
All three current winners keep their place on individual merit; none is beaten by a verified alternative on its own terms, but one pin is stale and the layer's deep gaps remain genuinely open pending a paid-entitlement decision outside this research task's scope.

alpaca-py (v0.44.0) is exactly current against both PyPI (upload_time 2026-08-11T10:15:07Z) and GitHub releases/latest (published 2026-08-11T10:11:55Z) -- confirmed by the incoming adversarial pass and independently reproducible. No free/open Python SDK substitutes for Alpaca's own API, and no rival (Massive, Databento, OpenBB) has an executed on-stack arm beating alpaca-py's measured 24,310,292-bar broad-universe acquisition (0 failed batches, 5,108 pages re-hashed, 0 mismatches; catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json trading[0]). The incoming packet's own adversarial check caught its own minor error (a pushed_at citation off by one calendar day); trivial, doesn't change the verdict.

exchange_calendars (4.13.2) is also exactly current; its 29 unreleased upstream commits, read in full, are dependency bumps, CI/lint and an AGENTS.md addition only -- no calendar-semantic change missed. New grounding this pass added: reading blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/sessions.py and runner.py directly shows exchange_calendars is wired into the live paper engine as an optional session-open fallback behind a primary hand-rolled session table, so this pick has a real (if secondary) effect on paper-lane session gating -- which raises the value of finally running the pandas_market_calendars comparison the layer's own decision text has deferred since at least 2026-09-23 ("should not be mixed" without one).

edgartools is the one winner that is stale, not challenged: its pin (v5.58.0, 2026-09-11) sits two releases behind upstream v5.59.1 (2026-09-26, independently reconfirmed today via gh api, exact timestamp match). Both missed releases are correctness fixes on exactly what this project uses the library for: v5.59.0 fixes seven 10-K/10-Q table-of-contents section-boundary bugs (an issuer's Item 7 wrongly returning Item 8 text); v5.59.1 fixes a same-day regression plus a bug where edgar_read returned zero 13F holdings for any filing, until hours before this review. The layer's hard, named gaps -- a survivorship-free universe, complete corporate actions (dividend currency), established historical point-in-time availability, and licensing/redistribution rights -- remain open, and every candidate that could plausibly close them is already known to this stack, not newly discovered today: Databento is already a "conditional" catalog card since at least 2026-09-22/23 (pin v0.86.0), and is itself now one release behind its own upstream v0.87.0 (released 2026-09-22, independently reconfirmed live today via pypi.org -- no further drift since the 0923 sweep, but the bump is still pending). trading.claude_summary: All six components the researcher packet treated as "current winners" (otelcol-contrib, prometheus, loki, grafana, restic, sandbox-runtime) earn their place on freshly checked, mostly-native evidence -- but the catalog's own bookkeeping (layers.json / catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json, checked_at 2026-09-22) actually records "winners": [] and "verdict_status": "pending_lanes", not a clean six-item list. Reading the actual adjudication file (evidence/artifacts/layer-verdicts-20260922/adjudication/us-equities-observability-hosting-20260922.json) shows why: it was a forced choice between two 2-component additions to otelcol-contrib -- set A (prometheus+loki) vs set B (sandbox-runtime+restic) -- and all 4 judgments split exactly along presentation order ("each... chose whichever return was shown as A"), a documented order-bias artifact, not an evidence disagreement; every judge's own text calls all four candidates well-evidenced. Grafana was in neither contested set (both lanes already agreed on it). Since prometheus/loki (telemetry storage) and sandbox-runtime/restic (sandbox+backup) answer different, non-overlapping scope terms the requirement names, the merit-based resolution is to keep all four together rather than pick a pair -- that alone resolves the "lanes disagreed" open_gap without new evidence. Two independent-verification findings during this review change the substantive picture: (1) restic's proven scope is broader than the researcher packet says -- two dated 2026-09-19 native_cli_e2e receipts I read directly (state-recovery/memory and state-recovery/qdrant, already cited by landscape/us-equities.json but omitted by the researcher) show live ai-memory SQLite and live Qdrant backup+restore with full integrity verification, not just the 22 static files the packet cites; off-host durability and Loki/Prometheus/broker-journal backup remain the real, still-open pieces. (2) I re-read the sandbox-runtime network-denial receipt myself rather than trusting the adversarial stage's account, and it holds up (dated 2026-09-25, independent review by a separately identified claude-opus-5-5 session, both "agree") -- but it tests generic loopback-HTTP egress denial, not "broker execution authority" specifically, which is this layer's own requirement text and the one clause no candidate has yet demonstrated. Separately, this repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep already ran two adversarial-review lenses over three candidates this task's researcher packet never mentioned: Grafana Tempo (survived, not refuted -- a real gap, since Claude Code already emits OTLP trace spans nothing currently ingests) and Presidio / Vector.dev (both refuted, with concrete reasons). The researcher packet also omitted Langfuse entirely despite it already being tracked as an "alternative" in this repo's own catalog. Net proposal: keep all six winners; add Grafana Tempo as a bounded trial candidate for the undemonstrated tracing gap; run the two concrete tests still open (re-validate the existing fixture against Prometheus v3.15.0 before bumping the pin one point release; exercise broker-execution-authority denial specifically, the missing half of sandbox-runtime's own overturn arm); leave the LLM-trace-observability candidates (Opik/SigNoz/Langfuse/Phoenix) as watch-only since none has native evidence and none beats an incumbent on this layer's actual scope. None of this moves a paper-lane number (engines run / paper acts passed / paper fills) -- it is infrastructure for the research harness itself, not the trading path.

trading.claude_summary: Portfolio-risk's only winner with native execution evidence remains skfolio, but the pinned artifact (1.2.9, WalkForward source c99fcf71349e2df4a7a1033ee85ca2e9ced9abee, accepted 2026-09-19 per blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/receipt.json) is verified stale: upstream shipped six releases in the seven days to 2026-09-26 (v1.3.0 through v1.4.0 -- a live PyPI check run today confirms 1.4.0 is still current, nothing newer has shipped), and I independently re-fetched all six GitHub release bodies via gh api. Two are named correctness fixes to value_at_risk (integer tail sizes, v1.3.3) and EVaR (log-sum-exp numerical stability, v1.3.4) -- exactly the "deterministic numeric risk" measures this layer exists to supply -- plus a new GeodesicShrinkageCovariance estimator (v1.3.0) and a multi-period sample-weight fix (v1.3.2). However, I also read the pinned commit's own _walk_forward.py source directly: it imports only sklearn.model_selection, sklearn.utils, skfolio.typing and skfolio.utils.tools -- never skfolio.measures or skfolio.moments -- so none of the six fixes touch the code path this repo has actually accepted. The staleness is real and dated but prospective: it matters once (still fully untested) skfolio optimizers or risk estimators run natively here, which remains an open gap either way. No competing library earns a verified advantage over skfolio for the accepted role. Riskfolio-Lib's "lacks a walk-forward/CV harness" knock was independently refuted here (its own readthedocs course page teaches Walk Forward, Cross-Validation and Combinatorial Purged CV, confirmed by a direct fetch), but it still ships no GitHub Releases object, hasn't tagged in ~4 months, and isn't sklearn-Pipeline/GridSearchCV-native. PyPortfolioOpt, cvxportfolio (GPL-3.0, 14-month-stale tag), fortitudo.tech (GPL-3.0), riskparityportfolio (PyPI 0.6.0 has no matching git tag -- verified provenance gap, latest tag is only v0.5.1), OptimalPortfolios and factorlasso (real, current, but single-maintainer-concentrated -- OptimalPortfolios' own pyproject.toml confirms it depends on both qis and factorlasso from the same author) all stay source-review-only with zero native execution in this repo. Two capability-additive, lower-confidence finds deserve a bounded trial rather than displacement: pyhrp offers a second, independently-authored HRP/Schur-complement implementation (real tests, coverage, MIT) to numerically cross-check skfolio's own HierarchicalRiskParity output -- exactly the "independent reconciliation" this layer's language asks for and nothing currently supplies; riskkit-quant is the only candidate in the whole set whose stated purpose is pre-trade position-sizing/stop enforcement (confirmed via its own repo description and 13 real test files), directly on point for this layer's most-repeated gap, though at 3 stars/single-maintainer/no third-party adoption it needs its own proof first. No candidate reviewed, including skfolio at any version, closes the layer's core gap: a verified connection from portfolio/risk-measure output to NautilusTrader's deterministic pre-trade enforcement or broker reconciliation. That gap is unchanged by this wave and stays open.

trading.claude_summary: Area definition (read directly from scratchpad/conv/layers.json): requirement text is "Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority" -- an agent/process-governance requirement, not primarily an SBOM/CVE/secret-scan requirement. trading.claude_summary: Winner DuckDB (data-duckdb, v1.5.5) earns its slot on merit, not incumbency: I independently re-verified the pin is still current on GitHub releases, GitHub tags and PyPI simultaneously (no v1.6.x anywhere) and found local, real (non-fixture) native-execution evidence the packet didn't cite — blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/README.md + receipt.json record a 45,406,248-event single-host study that "peaked at 13.1 GB resident memory with a 12 GB DuckDB limit." That is a genuine scale data point, not just an unmeasured gap. More importantly, this repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep (catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json) already fired two sharper, more targeted challengers at this exact layer than today's packet contains -- duckdb/ducklake (DuckDB's own multi-writer lakehouse extension) and xtdb/xtdb (bitemporal availability-rejection) -- and adversarially refuted both on concrete evidence (open DuckDB issues about lost deletes; Iceberg/ArcticDB already give comparable time-travel). No candidate in today's packet is better-evidenced than those two already-defeated ones. The layer's real open gap (no throughput/concurrency/multi-writer comparison exists) therefore stays open, and the layer's separate, larger requirement -- licensed rights, a survivorship-free universe, availability-rejection -- is a data-acquisition problem no storage engine choice fixes.\n\nDisposition: keep DuckDB; formally add the well-evidenced conditional alternatives with bounded trial plans rather than leaving them as informal notes. Dask and TimescaleDB are genuine beyond-inputs gap-fills (confirmed absent from repository-index.md/coverage.json before this pass) and both re-verified independently today (gh api + PyPI + a direct LICENSE-file read for TimescaleDB's Apache-2.0/tsl-Timescale-License split). ClickHouse, QuestDB, Iceberg and ArcticDB are already catalogued as "conditional" in catalogs/us-equities/data-research.json; I refreshed their pin currency and, for ArcticDB, read the actual Additional Use Grant clause (restricted term "Database Service" requires third parties controlling table schemas -- a solo internal research use does not appear to trigger it, though this is a primary-source reading, not legal sign-off, and the repo's existing licensor-check note still stands). Polars stays exactly where it already is (data-polars, decision "alternative," in-process SQL complement) -- nothing here challenges that, so it isn't listed as a challenger or rejected. Apache Spark, Ray, Turso, data.table, MarketStore and Tectonicdb are rejected below, each for a specific verified reason rather than because DuckDB currently holds the slot.

candidates.name: ClickHouse
candidates.demonstrated_gap: The layer's open gap is that no throughput, concurrency or multi-writer measurement exists for DuckDB or any server alternative. ClickHouse's MergeTree-family engines (ReplacingMergeTree confirmed in clickhouse.com docs) give shared multi-reader/multi-writer scans that a single embedded process structurally cannot, and the serverless clickhouse-local CLI allows a first comparison without a cluster. Separately, the catalog pin v26.8.7.19-lts is two LTS points behind v26.8.12.53-lts (published 2026-09-26), so a pin refresh is due whatever the adoption decision; the claimed v26.10.1.1-new release is an unpublished robot tag, not a release.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run clickhouse local at the refreshed pin v26.8.12.53-lts (no server) against the broad-universe daily.parquet, reproduce evaluate.py's aggregation, and diff the result hash plus wall-clock and peak RSS against the DuckDB receipt (13.1 GB peak, 12 GB limit). Pass: matching hash at equal-or-better memory or time. Escalate to a multi-process concurrent-writer test (two clients appending to one MergeTree table while a third reads) only if clickhouse-local shows an advantage; overturn DuckDB-as-sole-engine only if that concurrent test succeeds where an equivalent DuckDB multi-writer test is documented to fail.

trading.claude_summary: Layer has no adopted winner (layers.json: winners=[], decision="research", current_choice="Mover early-entry studies v1 and v2 found no development pass; Mover v3 core is preregistered and not frozen."). In-repo evidence, verified by reading the actual files: v1 ran 768 rule-exits and v2 ran 244 more (families E/F/P) on a frozen, cost-aware preregistered split -- 0/1012 pass net of costs (blueprints/us-equities/mover-early-entry/README.md; evidence/summary-dev-val-run-v1.json sha256 9d8c3d5b...; evidence/summary-v2-dev-val-run-v1.json sha256 75a5004b...). This falsifies naive long-only "detect an extreme mover, ride it" rules on this stack, and v3's own core draft (protocol-core-draft.json, status draft_pending_independent_pre_outcome_review, frozen_before_outcomes:false) is built on a literature-verified reversal/lottery-demand prior (Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw MAX effect), not a continuation prior. A separate, already-adversarially-verified sweep two days before this pass (catalogs/us-equities/mover-v3-sweep-20260924.json, 23 items) covers execution (Alpaca trailing_stop/OCO), halt/LULD data (databento/dbn normalized status schema) and several literature priors (days-to-cover, overnight/intraday tug-of-war) -- I cross-checked it and found no name overlap with this task's 15 candidates, so this pass is genuinely additive, not duplicative, with two exceptions folded into "rejected" below. No candidate anywhere meets the full compound requirement (detect+auto-size+auto-exit, preregistration-ready, US equities) as one system; the only full-shape system found is crypto/Bybit-scoped and off-requirement. The task's own adversarial-verification block was truncated after "kronos-repo-license-date"; I independently supplemented the gap via gh api / pypi.org / WebSearch / WebFetch (Kelly-Criterion, itch-book, Crypto Pump Scanner, Kronos re-check, the VPIN flash-crash controversy, and a direct re-fetch of the TLM abstract) rather than treating unverified claims as verified -- these are marked below.
